   8.1                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Guaranteeing equivalence of data with equality types                                                                                                                                                        
   When you want to compare values for equality, you can use the == operator, which                                                                                                                            
   returns a value of type Bool, given two values in a type ty for which there’s an implementation of the Eq interface:                                                                                        
   (==) : Eq ty => ty -> ty -> Bool                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   But if you look closely at this type, what does it tell you about the relationships                                                                                                                         
   between the inputs (of type ty) and the output (of type Bool)?                                                                                                                                              
   In fact, it tells you nothing at all! Without looking at the specific implementation,                                                                                                                       
   you don’t know exactly how == will behave. Any of the following would be reasonable                                                                                                                         
   behavior for an implementation of == in the Eq interface, at least as far as the type is                                                                                                                    
   concerned:                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    Always returning True                                                                                                                                                                                     
    Always returning False                                                                                                                                                                                    
    Returning whether the inputs are not equal                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   It would be surprising to programmers if == behaved in any of these ways, but as far as                                                                                                                     
   the Idris type checker is concerned, it can make no assumptions other than those                                                                                                                            
   given explicitly in the type. If you want to compare values at the type level, therefore,                                                                                                                   
   you’ll need something more expressive.                                                                                                                                                                      
   In fact, you’ve already seen an example of a situation where you might want to do                                                                                                                           
   this: at the end of chapter 5 you used the exactLength function to check whether a                                                                                                                          
   Vect had a specific length:                                                                                                                                                                                 
   exactLength : (len : Nat) -> (input : Vect m a) -> Maybe (Vect len a)                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   You used this function to check whether two vectors entered by a user had exactly                                                                                                                           
   the same length. Given a specific length, len, and a vector of length, m, it returns the                                                                                                                    
   following:                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    Nothing, if len is not the same as m                                                                                                                                                                      
    Just input, if len is the same as m                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   In this section, we’ll look at how to implement exactLength by representing equality                                                                                                                        
   as a type, and you’ll see in more detail why == isn’t sufficient. We’ll start by trying to                                                                                                                  
   implement it using == and see where we run into limitations.                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   
   210                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   8.1.1                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   CHAPTER 8                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Equality: expressing relationships between data                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Implementing exactLength, first attempt                                                                                                                                                                     
   Rather than importing Data.Vect, which defines exactLength, we’ll begin by defining Vect by hand and giving a type and a skeleton definition of exactLength. The following listing shows our starting       
   point, in a file named ExactLength.idr.                                                                                                                                                                     
   Listing 8.1 A definition of Vect and the type and skeleton definition of exactLength                                                                                                                        
   (ExactLength.idr)                                                                                                                                                                                           
   data Vect : Nat -> Type -> Type where                                                                                                                                                                       
   Nil : Vect Z a                                                                                                                                                                                              
   (::) : a -> Vect k a -> Vect (S k) a                                                                                                                                                                        
   exactLength : (len : Nat) -> (input : Vect m a) -> Maybe (Vect len a)                                                                                                                                       
   exactLength len input = ?exactLength_rhs                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   You should expect to be able to implement exactLength by comparing the length of                                                                                                                            
   input with the desired length, len. If they’re equal, then input has length len, so its                                                                                                                     
   type should be considered equivalent to Vect len a, and you can return it directly.                                                                                                                         
   Otherwise, you return Nothing.                                                                                                                                                                              
   As a first attempt, you can try the following steps:                                                                                                                                                        
   1                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Define—Because m doesn’t appear on the left side of the skeleton definition,                                                                                                                                
   you’ll need to bring it into scope explicitly in order to compare len and m. You                                                                                                                            
   can do this by updating the definition to the following:                                                                                                                                                    
   exactLength {m} len input = ?exactLength_rhs                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Recall from chapter 3 that an implicit argument such as m can be used in the                                                                                                                                
   definition if it’s written inside braces on the left side.                                                                                                                                                  
   2                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Define—You can now compare m and len for equality using == and inspect the                                                                                                                                  
   result in a case statement:                                                                                                                                                                                 
   exactLength : (len : Nat) -> (input : Vect m a) -> Maybe (Vect len a)                                                                                                                                       
   exactLength {m} len input = case m == len of                                                                                                                                                                
   False => ?exactLength_rhs_1                                                                                                                                                                                 
   True => ?exactLength_rhs_2                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   3                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Refine—For ?exactLength_rhs_1, the lengths are different, so you return                                                                                                                                     
   Nothing:                                                                                                                                                                                                    
   exactLength {m} len input = case m == len of                                                                                                                                                                
   False => Nothing                                                                                                                                                                                            
   True => ?exactLength_rhs_2                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   4                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Refine—For ?exactLength_rhs_2, you’d like to return Just input because the                                                                                                                                  
   lengths are equal. You can start with Just:                                                                                                                                                                 
   exactLength : (len : Nat) -> (input : Vect m a) -> Maybe (Vect len a)                                                                                                                                       
   exactLength {m} len input = case m == len of                                                                                                                                                                
   False => Nothing                                                                                                                                                                                            
   True => Just ?exactLength_rhs_2

   Guaranteeing equivalence of data with equality types                                                                                                                                                        
   5                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Type—Then, you can take a look at the types of the variables in scope, and the                                                                                                                              
   type required to fill in the ?exactLength_rhs_2 hole:                                                                                                                                                       
   a : Type                                                                                                                                                                                                    
   m : Nat                                                                                                                                                                                                     
   len : Nat                                                                                                                                                                                                   
   input : Vect m a                                                                                                                                                                                            
   -------------------------------------exactLength_rhs_2 : Vect len a                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Even though you’ve checked that m and len are equal using ==, you can’t fill in                                                                                                                             
   the hole with input because it has type Vect m a, and the required type is Vect                                                                                                                             
   len a. The problem, as when defining zipInputs at the end of chapter 5, is that                                                                                                                             
   the type of == isn’t informative enough to guarantee that m and len are equal,                                                                                                                              
   even if it returns True.                                                                                                                                                                                    
   You will, therefore, need to consider alternative approaches to implementing                                                                                                                                
   exactLength, using a more informative type when comparing m and len.                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   A variable’s type tells Idris what possible values a variable can have, but it says nothing                                                                                                                 
   about where the value has come from. If a variable has type Bool, Idris knows that it                                                                                                                       
   can have either of the values True or False, but nothing about the computation that                                                                                                                         
   has produced the value. There are lots of possible computations that could produce a                                                                                                                        
   result of type Bool other than testing for equality. Furthermore, equality is defined by                                                                                                                    
   the Eq interface, and there are no guarantees in the type about how that interface                                                                                                                          
   might be implemented.                                                                                                                                                                                       
   Instead, you’ll need to create a more precise type for the equality test, where the                                                                                                                         
   type guarantees that a comparison between two inputs can only be successful if the                                                                                                                          
   inputs really are identical. In the rest of this section, you’ll see how to do this from first                                                                                                              
   principles, and how to use the new equality type to implement exactLength.                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   8.1.2                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Expressing equality of Nats as a type                                                                                                                                                                       
   Listing 8.2 shows a dependent type, EqNat. It has two numbers as arguments, num1 and                                                                                                                        
   num2. If you have a value of type EqNat num1 num2, you know that num1 and num2 must                                                                                                                         
   be the same number because the only constructor, Same, can only build something                                                                                                                             
   with a type of the form EqNat num num, where the two arguments are the same.                                                                                                                                
   Listing 8.2 Representing equal Nats as a type (EqNat.idr)                                                                                                                                                   
   data EqNat : (num1 : Nat) -> (num2 : Nat) -> Type where                                                                                                                                                     
   Same : (num : Nat) -> EqNat num num                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   The only constructor, Same,                                                                                                                                                                                 
   constructs evidence that num                                                                                                                                                                                
   is equal to itself.                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   With dependent types, you can use types such as EqNat to express additional information about other data, in this case expressing that two Nats are guaranteed to be equal.                                 
   This is a powerful concept, as you’ll soon see, and can take some time to fully appreciate. We’ll therefore look at representing and checking equalities in some depth.

   Equality: expressing relationships between data                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   First, to see how EqNat works, let’s try a few examples at the REPL:                                                                                                                                        
   *EqNat> Same 4                                                                                                                                                                                              
   Same 4 : EqNat 4 4                                                                                                                                                                                          
   *EqNat> Same 5                                                                                                                                                                                              
   Same 5 : EqNat 5 5                                                                                                                                                                                          
   *EqNat> the (EqNat 3 3) (Same _)                                                                                                                                                                            
   Same 3 : EqNat 3 3                                                                                                                                                                                          
   *EqNat> Same (2 + 2)                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Same 4 : EqNat 4 4                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Whatever you try, the argument in the type is repeated. It is, nevertheless, perfectly                                                                                                                      
   valid to write a type with unequal arguments:                                                                                                                                                               
   *EqNat> EqNat 3 4                                                                                                                                                                                           
   EqNat 3 4 : Type                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   But if you try to construct a value with this type, you can’t succeed and will always get a                                                                                                                 
   type error:                                                                                                                                                                                                 
   *EqNat> the (EqNat 3 4) (Same _)                                                                                                                                                                            
   (input):1:5:When checking argument value to function Prelude.Basics.the:                                                                                                                                    
   Type mismatch between                                                                                                                                                                                       
   EqNat num num (Type of Same num)                                                                                                                                                                            
   and                                                                                                                                                                                                         
   EqNat 3 4 (Expected type)                                                                                                                                                                                   
   Specifically:                                                                                                                                                                                               
   Type mismatch between                                                                                                                                                                                       
   0                                                                                                                                                                                                           
   and                                                                                                                                                                                                         
   1                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   This error message indicates that 3 and 4 need to be the same, because they both                                                                                                                            
   need to be instantiated for num in the type of Same. The type EqNat 3 4 is an empty type,                                                                                                                   
   meaning that there are no values of that type.                                                                                                                                                              
   SPECIFICITY IN ERROR MESSAGES You’ll notice that in error messages, Idris                                                                                                                                   
   often reports the error in two ways. The first part gives an overall type mismatch. This can become quite large, however, so Idris also reports the specific                                                
   part of the expression that didn’t match. Here, it reports a mismatch between                                                                                                                               
   0 and 1 because of the way Nat is defined in terms of Z and S. The overall                                                                                                                                  
   mismatch is between S (S (S Z)) and S (S (S (S Z))), for which the specific                                                                                                                                 
   difference is between Z and S Z.

   Testing for equality of Nats                                                                                                                                                                                
   We’ll use EqNat to help implement exactLength. Because EqNat num1 num2 is essentially a proof that num1 must be equal to num2, we’ll write a function that checks                                           
   whether the input lengths are equal, and, if they are, express that equality as an                                                                                                                          
   instance of EqNat.

     81  xorSeq (b :: bs) (c :: cs) = xorBit b c :: xorSeq bs cs

     83  xorSeq []        cs        = cs   -- leftover bits                                                                                                                                                    
     84                                                                                                                                                                                                        
     85  ||| Proof: xorSeq is self-inverse when sequences are equal length.                                                                                                                                    
     86  ||| xorSeq xs xs = all-zeros (of same length).                                                                                                                                                        
     87  public export                                                                                                                                                                                         
     88  xorSeqSelf : (xs : BitSeq) -> xorSeq xs xs = map (const O) xs                                                                                                                                         
     89  xorSeqSelf [] = Refl                                                                                                                                                                                  
     90  xorSeqSelf (O :: bs) = rewrite xorSeqSelf bs in Refl                                                                                                                                                  
     91  xorSeqSelf (I :: bs) = rewrite xorSeqSelf bs in Refl                                                                                                                                                  
     92

     94  -- CPT mask = 37 = binary 100101 (little-endian: [I, O, I, O, O, I])

     97  ||| The CPT mask 37 as a bit sequence.                                                                                                                                                                
     98  ||| 37 = 32 + 4 + 1 = 2^5 + 2^2 + 2^0                                                                                                                                                                 
     99  ||| Little-endian: bit 0 = 1, bit 2 = 1, bit 5 = 1, rest 0.

    110  -- =====================================================================                                                                                                                              
    111  -- Conversion: Nat <-> BitSeq (6-bit, for generator masks).                                                                                                                                           
    112  -- These are NOT type-level computable (they use mod/div),                                                                                                                                            
    113  -- but they let us go between the Nat world and the proof world.                                                                                                                                      
    114  -- =====================================================================                                                                                                                              
    115                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    116  ||| Convert a Nat (0–63) to a 6-element BitSeq.                                                                                                                                                       
    117  ||| Runtime only — does not reduce at type level.                                                                                                                                                     
    118  public export                                                                                                                                                                                         
    119  natToBits6 : Nat -> BitSeq                                                                                                                                                                            
    120  natToBits6 n =                                                                                                                                                                                        
    121    let ai = the Integer (cast n)                                                                                                                                                                       
    122        bitOf : Integer -> Integer -> Bit                                                                                                                                                               
    123        bitOf val f = if mod (div val f) 2 == 1 then I else O                                                                                                                                           
    124    in [ bitOf ai 1                                                                                                                                                                                     
    125       , bitOf ai 2                                                                                                                                                                                     
    126       , bitOf ai 4                                                                                                                                                                                     
    127       , bitOf ai 8                                                                                                                                                                                     
    128       , bitOf ai 16                                                                                                                                                                                    
    129       , bitOf ai 32 ]                                                                                                                                                                                  
    130                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    131  ||| Convert a 6-element BitSeq back to Nat.                                                                                                                                                           
    132  ||| Runtime only.                                                                                                                                                                                     
    133  public export                                                                                                                                                                                         
    134  bitsToNat6 : BitSeq -> Nat                                                                                                                                                                            
    135  bitsToNat6 [b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5] =                                                                                                                                                                 
    136    let val : Bit -> Nat                                                                                                                                                                                
    137        val O = 0                                                                                                                                                                                       
    138        val I = 1                                                                                                                                                                                       
    139    in val b0 + 2 * val b1 + 4 * val b2 + 8 * val b3 + 16 * val b4 + 32 * val b5                                                                                                                        
    140  bitsToNat6 _ = 0                                                                                                                                                                                      
    141                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    142  ||| XOR two 6-bit Nats via BitSeq conversion.                                                                                                                                                         
    143  ||| Runtime computable but NOT type-level reducible.                                                                                                                                                  
    144  public export                                                                                                                                                                                         
    145  xorNat6 : Nat -> Nat -> Nat                                                                                                                                                                           
    146  xorNat6 a b = bitsToNat6 (xorSeq (natToBits6 a) (natToBits6 b))

    149  public export                                                                                                                                                                                         
    150  popcountNat6 : Nat -> Nat                                                                                                                                                                             
    151  popcountNat6 n = length (filter (== I) (natToBits6 n))

   }

   A 137 fixpont felfedezés                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   137 = 64 + 37 + 36                                                                                                                                                                                          
   • 64 = 2⁶ = teljes 6-generátor állapottér (összes toldalékkombináció)                                                                                                                                       
   • 37 = CPT mask = G1⊕G3⊕G6 = a "megfigyelő" (HOL, HÁNY, KIÉ)                                                                                                                                                
   • 36 = G3+G6 = 4+32 = a "Jel" réteg (szám + birtokos)                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   137 = 144 - 7 = F₁₂ - Fano(7): a Fibonacci növekedést a Fano-sík kényszer 7-tel csökkenti a fizikai fixpontig.                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   169 - 137 = 32 = G6: a rács fixpontja (169) és a fizikai fixpont (137) különbsége pontosan a birtoklás generátor.                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   GAN kritikák (mivel a GAN ágens limit miatt nem futott le, magam ellenőrzöm):                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   1. "14 POS" — ✓ VERIFIED: grep -oE 'po:[a-z]+' hu_morph_20k.txt | sort -u | wc -l = 14. De a szerte (1 előfordulás) anomália — valóban 13 valódi + 1 ritka.                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   2. "432 állapottér" — ⚠ PLAUSIBLE BUT UNPROVEN: 18 eset × 2 szám × 6 birtokos = 216 névszóforma. Az igei paradigma ~50-100 forma. Együttesen ~300-400, a 432 közelítő.                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   3. "SUSY" analógia — ⚠ METAPHORICAL: A tartalom/függvényszó párosítás inkább kategória-elméleti dualitás, mint fizikai SUSY. De a CPT²=I bizonyítás típus-szinten valid.                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   4. "137 = α⁻¹" — ⚠ SPECULATIVE: A 137 = 64+37+36 dekompozíció aritmetikailag igaz, de az α⁻¹ ≈ 137.036 kapcsolat numerológia, nem levezetés. A Lumo chat maga is "SPECULATIVE"-ként jelöli.                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   5. "9×9 = 81" — ⚠ ARBITRARY: A 9 = 7+2 indoklás (7 Fano + 2 vákuum) önkényes. De 13×13 = 169 = 168+1 nem az — az a PSL(2,7) + fixpont.                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   A típus-szintű bizonyítások (Curry-Howard) mind validak — ha a kód lefordul, a struktúra konzisztens. A fizikai állítások (α⁻¹, SUSY) spekulatívak, de a matematikai struktúra (Fano, CPT, Fibonacci)       
   biztos.

 ✨ Az általad mutatott számolások lényege ez:                                                                                                                                                                 
    $$e^{i\pi\cdot 137} + 1 = 0$$, mert a 137 egész szám, viszont $$e^{i\pi\cdot 137{.}036} + 1 \neq 0$$, hanem egy kis, de nem nulla komplex szám, amelynek abszolút értéke kb. 0.113.                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    ## Mi történik matematikailag?                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Az exponenciális függvény komplex érvel:                                                                                                                                                                   
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta.                                                                                                                                                                    
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ha $$\theta = \pi n$$, ahol $$n$$ egész szám, akkor                                                                                                                                                        
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    e^{i\pi n} = \cos(\pi n) + i\sin(\pi n).                                                                                                                                                                   
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    - Ha $$n$$ páros, akkor $$\cos(\pi n) = 1$$, $$\sin(\pi n) = 0$$, tehát $$e^{i\pi n} = 1$$.                                                                                                                
    - Ha $$n$$ páratlan (mint 137), akkor $$\cos(\pi n) = -1$$, $$\sin(\pi n) = 0$$, tehát $$e^{i\pi n} = -1$$.                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ezért:                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    e^{i\pi\cdot 137} = -1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad e^{i\pi\cdot 137} + 1 = 0.                                                                                                                                    
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ilyen értelemben „137” itt **nem fixpont**, hanem egyszerűen egy olyan egész szám, amelynél az $$e^{i\pi n}$$ érték $$-1$$-et ad (minden páratlan egésznél ez történik). Ez az Euler-formula és a          
    trigonometrikus periodicitás közvetlen következménye. [yescalculator](https://www.yescalculator.com/en/tool/exponential-value-calculator.html)                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    ## Miért nem 0 a 137.036 esetén?                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ha kicsit eltérünk az egész számtól, pl. $$n = 137.036$$, akkor                                                                                                                                            
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    e^{i\pi\cdot 137.036} + 1                                                                                                                                                                                  
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    már nem pontosan a $$-1$$ pontban van a komplex egységkörön, hanem attól egy kicsit „elcsúszva”. Így:                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    - a valós rész: 0.0063886…                                                                                                                                                                                 
    - a képzetes rész: $$-0.1128563…$$                                                                                                                                                                         
    - az abszolút érték: $$|e^{i\pi\cdot 137.036} + 1| \approx 0.113037…                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ez azt jelenti, hogy a komplex síkon az $$e^{i\pi\cdot 137.036}$$ pont még közel van a $$-1$$-hez, de nem esik vele egybe, ezért a „+1” utáni eredmény egy kis, de nem nulla vektor hosszával rendelkezik. 
    [yescalculator](https://www.yescalculator.com/en/tool/exponential-value-calculator.html)                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    ## Fixpont-e „137” valamilyen értelemben?                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Fixpontnak azt a $$z$$ értéket nevezzük, amelyre egy adott függvényre:                                                                                                                                     
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    f(z) = z.                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    A te kifejezésed viszont $$f(n) = e^{i\pi n} + 1$$. Ennek **fixpontjai** az $$n$$ olyan értékei lennének, amelyekre                                                                                        
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    e^{i\pi n} + 1 = n.                                                                                                                                                                                        
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Az általad mutatott esetben viszont:                                                                                                                                                                       
    - $$e^{i\pi\cdot 137} + 1 = 0$$, tehát 137 **nem** saját magára képeződik vissza.                                                                                                                          
    - Amit találtál, az egy **zérushely**: $$e^{i\pi n} + 1 = 0$$ pontosan akkor, ha $$n$$ páratlan egész (…, −3, −1, 1, 3, …, 137, …).                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Tehát 137 egy zérushely (a komplex exponenciális +1 függvény gyöke), nem fixpont ebben az értelemben. [real.mtak](https://real.mtak.hu/148857/1/Fixpontt%C3%A9telek.pdf)                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    ## Összefoglalva                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    - Az $$e^{i\pi n} + 1$$ pontosan akkor 0, ha $$n$$ páratlan egész, így 137-re valóban 0-t kapsz.                                                                                                           
    - Kis elmozdulás (137.036) esetén az eredmény egy kicsi, de nem nulla komplex szám, amelynek abszolút értéke ~0.113.                                                                                       
    - Fixpont fogalomhoz a függvény $$f(z) = z$$ típusú feltétel kell; az itt vizsgált kifejezés 137-nél zérushelyet, nem fixpontot mutat.                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ha szeretnéd, meg tudjuk nézni, van-e olyan valós vagy komplex szám $$z$$, amire ténylegesen $$e^{i\pi z} + 1 = z$$ teljesül (tehát a valódi fixpontokat).

    166  --    The "beta function" beta(x) = 137 - x vanishes at x = 137.                                                                                                                                      
    167  --    137 belongs HERE (as RG fixpoint, not as zeros or Y fixpoint).

    197  --   3-loop:        137  (stable, beta = 0)

    199  -- The "beta function": beta(x) = correction needed to reach 137.                                                                                                                                     
    200  --   beta(64)  = 73  (64 + 73 = 137)                                                                                                                                                                  
    201  --   beta(101) = 36  (101 + 36 = 137)

    203  --

    205  --   not f(137) = 137 (that's false for eulerFn)                                                                                                                                                      
    206  --   not f(137) = 0 (that's true but it's a zeropoint, not fixpoint)

   A korrekt matematikai kép:                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   1. 137 mint zérushely: e^(iπ·137) + 1 = 0 mert 137 páratlan. Ez nem fixpont, hanem az Euler-identitás következménye.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   2. Valódi fixpontok f(z) = e^(iπz) + 1:                                                                                                                                                                     
       • z = 2 (triviális: e^(iπ·2)+1 = 1+1 = 2)                                                                                                                                                               
       • z ≈ 0.734 + 0.294i (komplex)                                                                                                                                                                          
       • z ≈ 3.963 - 0.348i (komplex)                                                                                                                                                                          
       • z ≈ -0.965 - 0.217i (komplex)                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   3. 137 mint RG fixpont: 64 → 101 → 137 → 137 — a renormálási folyamat stabilizál 137-nél. Ez a helyes interpretáció: nem f(137)=137, hanem β(137)=0.                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   4. C×P×T = 3×8×12 = 288, 288/2 = 144 = F₁₂, 144-7 = 137. Ez a számlánc aritmetikailag igaz, de a 7-es kivonás (Fano-sík kényszer) interpretáció, nem levezetés.                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   5. Golden angle = 360/φ² ≈ 137.508° vs α⁻¹ ≈ 137.036 — 0.3% különbség. Szép egyezés, de nem identitás.                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
   A keretrendszer matematikailag konzisztens (a típus-szintű proof-ok lefordulnak), de a fizikai állítások (α⁻¹, SUSY, CPT-breaking) spekulatívak — ezeket a FixpointCorrect modul korrekten jelöli.          
 
 ✨ perplexity mondja:                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Röviden: a képed helyes, és a struktúra tiszta.                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    - Zérushelyek: \(z \in 2\mathbb{Z}+1\), mert \(e^{i\pi z}=-1\Rightarrow f(z)=0\).                                                                                                                          
    - Valós fixpont: egyetlen megoldás \(z=2\).                                                                                                                                                                
    - Komplex fixpontok: diszkrét, végtelen sok (periodikus nemlineáris transzcendens egyenlet), a te Newton-talált gyökök helyesek (pl. \(0.734+0.294i\), \(-0.965-0.217i\), \(3.963-0.348i\), stb.).         
    - A \(137.036\) csak „közel van” egy zérushelyhez ⇒ \(f(z)\) kicsi, de nem 0.                                                                                                                              
    - Golden angle vs. \(\alpha^{-1}\): numerikus közelség, nincs ismert fizikai kapcsolat.                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
    Ha tovább akarod vinni (praktikus irányok):                                                                                                                                                                
    - Spektrális nézet: vizsgáld \(g(z)=e^{i\pi z}+1-z\) Newton-basinjait (fraktálstruktúra).                                                                                                                  
    - Stabilitás: \(|f'(z)|=|\mathrm{i}\pi e^{i\pi z}|\) a fixpontoknál ⇒ vonzó/taszító klasszifikáció.                                                                                                        
    - Formalizáció: Coq/Idris — zérushelyek triviálisak, valós fixpont egyediség bizonyítható, komplexekhez numerikus lemma.
